epistemic_purpose: determine whether a background-terminal event must resume outstanding agent work, then repair only the proven re-entry seam

product_contract.doctrine_evidence: sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/definitions.ts:669-676: 'For long-running commands, run them in background and redirect output to a tmp file that you can read from later.'
product_contract.doctrine_summary: Contract A (model-driven polling) for the model; Contract C (user-return after detach) for the runtime. No Contract B (automatic re-entry) for the run_commands path.

reproduction.red_note: The AGCONT-CTL-01..07 control tests prove the runtime's behavior is consistent with the doctrine. There is no automatic agent re-entry on background-command terminal events. The defect is a model-side failure to follow the F4 doctrine (the model yielded control prematurely).

causality.ablation_note: AC1 and AC2 ablations are not applicable because the AC3 classification does not require a runtime re-entry obligation. The F4 doctrine places the polling obligation on the model, not the runtime.

repair.rationale: Per ACT section 50 stop rule: 'If the runtime proves the agent turn was genuinely complete: CASE_AC3. STOP. Do not invent automatic agent resurrection.' The AGCONT01 focused test proves the runtime's behavior is consistent with the F4 doctrine. Adding any 'terminal wakes model' mechanism would violate conservation C2 (fire-and-forget must not resurrect completed agent) and the ACT's stop rule.

live_qualification.rationale: AC3 classification: the runtime does not promise automatic agent re-entry. No live qualification is needed. The AGCONT01 focused test family substitutes for live qualification by exercising the real production seams (CommandJobManager + SdkSessionEventCoordinator + TurnStateTracker + Controller.maybeReevaluateDeferredContinuation) and asserting the absence of agent re-entry across 7 control scenarios.

doctrine_bound.f4_text: For long-running commands, run them in background and redirect output to a tmp file that you can read from later.
doctrine_bound.implication_for_user_request: When the user asks 'wait until it finishes', the model is responsible for polling the background command's output (via another run_commands call to read the tmp log). The runtime does not promise to re-invoke the model.

tests: AGCONT-CTL-01 (GREEN): deferral + natural terminal commits awaiting_followup WITHOUT invoking the agent runtime
AGCONT-CTL-02 (GREEN): explicit user follow-up is the canonical re-entry path (not terminal-driven)
AGCONT-CTL-03 (GREEN): start-and-return task does NOT trigger agent re-entry on later terminal (conservation C2)
AGCONT-CTL-04 (GREEN): no background dependency -> no deferred marker -> no later re-entry (conservation C4)
AGCONT-CTL-05 (GREEN): newer turn start clears deferred marker; late terminal cannot resurrect (conservation C3)
AGCONT-CTL-06 (GREEN): terminal bridge fires exactly once per >0->0 cardinal transition (conservation C5)
AGCONT-CTL-07 (GREEN): terminal of a different session's job does NOT wake this session (conservation C4)
